title: Scope context
statement: The platform shall scope operations by organization and, where applicable, branch.
accept: Products and customers are shared within an organization; orders, movements and events are branch-scoped. Switching branch clears prior cart and camera session state. Authorized membership enforcement is required for R1.

title: Identity and access
source: I Authentication Roles and Security; G1 2.5.3; G2 2.5.3
statement: The pilot shall authenticate users and enforce role and branch permissions on every protected operation.
accept: Deny anonymous and unauthorized access server-side; test session expiry, logout, recovery, administrator MFA and cross-tenant object IDs. Provider choice is pending.

title: Product catalogue
statement: The platform shall maintain unique organization SKU, name, selling price and unit cost.
accept: Reject blank identifiers and negative prices; store monetary values as integer paisa. Variants, barcodes, taxes, units, batches, expiry and channel prices require later acceptance cases.

title: Stock ledger
statement: Stock changes shall append signed movements with quantity, reason and unique reference.
accept: Reject zero/noninteger quantity, unknown SKU and reductions below reservations. Repeating the same reference and payload is a no-op; a different payload fails. SQL UPDATE/DELETE of movements fails.

title: Reservations
source: I Inventory and Warehouse Management; Omnichannel Order Management
statement: Uncompleted, uncancelled orders shall reserve stock and reduce available-to-sell quantity.
accept: On-hand equals signed movement sum; available equals on-hand minus active reservations. Two competing orders cannot oversell. Failed delivery retains reservation until completion or cancellation.

title: Checkout
statement: Checkout shall validate each cart item and commit order, stock deduction, loyalty and audit atomically for a completed POS sale.
accept: Empty carts, nonpositive quantities, insufficient stock and POS COD fail without partial writes. Retry returns the original order only when its original payload matches. Advanced POS features are AP-27.

title: Payment record
source: I Advanced Smart POS Payment methods
statement: R0 shall record cash, externally paid or COD arrangements without storing payment-card secrets.
accept: Require operator confirmation in the UI; reject COD for immediate POS checkout. External paid means a recorded external payment, not gateway verification. Signed provider confirmation is required in R2.

title: Order fulfillment
source: I Omnichannel Order Management; Delivery Management
statement: Orders shall progress through the permitted state machine and maintain reservations until resolved.
accept: Reject skipped states. Dispatch requires rider text; completion from dispatched requires proof; COD completion requires collection confirmation. GPS, rider accounts and cash settlement remain planned.

title: Customer loyalty
statement: The platform shall register organization-scoped customers and accrue points on completed orders.
accept: Unknown customer is rejected at checkout. Award floor(total paisa / 10000) points once per order. Redemption, tiers, consent, segmentation, refunds and rewards remain planned.

title: Audit and attribution
source: I Administration Reliability and System Operations; G1 2.5.3
statement: State-changing business actions shall be auditable with scope, time, reference and actor.
accept: Existing order create/transition records are transactional. R1 must add authenticated actor, override justification, configuration/catalogue actions and access-controlled retention; stock reasons alone do not provide complete audit coverage.

title: Sales import
statement: Forecast intake shall accept CSV/JSON with date, sku, store_id, sales_qty, unit_price and promotion_flag, supporting SKU/price aliases.
accept: Reject invalid dates, missing identifiers, negative numeric values and nonbinary flags. Validate six calendar months per group for forecasting. Rejected import must not overwrite usable history.

title: Daily history
statement: Forecasting shall operate on a single SKU/store with continuous daily observations.
accept: Aggregate same-day sales; do not silently fill unknown dates with zero. Require explicit zero-sales rows. Reject mixed groups and history shorter than six months. Report source and selected group.

title: Forecast generation
statement: The product shall generate nonnegative forecasts for 7, 14 or 30 days using the approved model baseline.
accept: Current seasonal naive, LightGBM, Prophet and equal-weight ensemble produce dates after the last observation. ARIMA/LSTM specified in G1 are absent; revision requires approval. Missing model dependency produces a clear error.

title: Model evaluation
statement: Every forecast shall show holdout MAE/RMSE/MAPE and clearly labeled nominal uncertainty intervals.
accept: Keep final 30 days out of evaluation training. MAPE excludes zero actuals and is unavailable if all are zero. Current intervals use residual quantiles; measured 95% coverage is not established.

title: Retraining and review
statement: The system shall flag poor model quality and provide a controlled retraining workflow.
accept: Current generation trains on demand and warns for MAPE above 15% or unavailable. Scheduled change detection, durable model versions, automated retraining and rollback need implementation and failure/replay tests.

title: Inventory decisions
source: G1 REQ-SF2-1 to REQ-SF2-3 and REQ-SF3-2
statement: The system shall compute EOQ, safety stock, reorder point and days of supply from history, stock and explicit costs.
accept: Reject invalid/nonfinite costs and lead times; flag stock below reorder point or under seven days supply. Zero demand returns no numeric days-of-supply. Promotion/overstock-risk alerts are not complete.

title: ABC classification
statement: ABC classification shall rank SKU revenue using cumulative value thresholds of 80% and 95%.
accept: Top SKU remains A even when crossing 80%; item percentages are measured, not forced. Quarterly scheduling is pending. Record this interpretation as a clarification of the original fixed item-share wording.

title: Scenario analysis
statement: Decision support shall distinguish historical inventory-policy simulation from price or promotion scenario modeling.
accept: Current simulator counts each arrival once and unmet demand as shortage, using prior data for default rules. Price elasticity, promotional counterfactuals and causal savings claims require separate implementation and validation.

title: Reporting
source: G1 REQ-SF3-1 and REQ-SF3-4; I Unified Analytics
statement: Reports shall identify scope, period, units, source and model where relevant and export real CSV, XLSX or PDF.
accept: Verify signatures and readable output. Sales/ABC filters apply date ranges; saved forecast/plan/simulation exports use saved analysis. Full turnover charts and configurable branding remain pending.

title: Video perception
statement: Vision shall process authorized video/RTSP sources and pass timestamped boxes and anonymous track IDs to analytics.
accept: Current YOLO/ByteTrack implementation must pass camera disconnect and model failure tests. DeepSORT, 1–16 stream capacity, 95% mAP and MOTA targets are unverified or unmet as specified.

title: Zones and movement
statement: Users shall configure camera polygons and review zone occupancy, dwell and heatmaps.
accept: Persist camera zones within scope and reject invalid polygons. Test known trajectories at boundaries. Fixed 15-minute/hour/day aggregation and 90% dwell accuracy require separate evaluation.

title: Activity alerts
statement: Vision shall produce reviewable loitering, restricted-zone and shelf-interaction observations using configurable thresholds.
accept: Evaluate threshold crossings and cooldown on labeled clips. Default source targets include 120-second loitering and 30-second shelf interaction. Dedicated unattended-staff checkout after 60 seconds is planned.

title: Event timeline
statement: Events shall support scoped date/camera/text filters and durable acknowledgement with 30-day metadata retention.
accept: Storage acknowledgement must survive reopening. UI must read acknowledged_at consistently; current UI reads acknowledged and needs correction. Query excludes expired events; pruning occurs on initialization/save, not a timer.

title: Evidence and delivery
statement: Alerts shall expose available evidence and export authorized event records; real-time delivery shall be measured.
accept: Filtered CSV exists. Snapshot/video retention, full vision PDF reports, push delivery under 500 ms and simultaneous-user access require implementation or validation. Streamlit WebSocket transport alone is not an event delivery SLA.

title: Supplier purchasing
statement: The platform shall manage suppliers, approvals, purchase orders, receiving, costs, returns and balances.
accept: Partial receipts create only the received stock movement; duplicate receipts do not duplicate inventory. Recommended orders require authorized human approval and reconciliation to supplier invoice.

title: Warehouses and transfers
statement: The platform shall support locations, stock counts, transfer states, batches, expiry and valuation.
accept: A transfer records paired source/destination movements with in-transit status and exception handling. Count corrections preserve history; damaged/expired stock cannot silently become sellable.

title: Advanced POS
statement: POS shall support approved discounts, shifts, receipts, returns, hardware and offline reconciliation as separate capabilities.
accept: Manager override is attributed; returns cannot exceed original sold quantity; offline replay is idempotent. Barcode/scale/printer compatibility and tax calculations require explicit device and jurisdiction acceptance.

title: External orders and delivery
source: I Omnichannel Order Management; Delivery Management
statement: Official connectors shall import orders, synchronize availability and reconcile delivery/payment states.
accept: Authenticate webhook origin, deduplicate provider event IDs, handle out-of-order updates and record settlement differences. Merchant API access is a prerequisite; do not infer it from a provider name.

title: Storefront and social commerce
source: I Web Mobile App and Social Commerce
statement: Customer channels shall offer catalogue, checkout, order status and permitted communications.
accept: Public customers cannot see another account or branch inventory beyond policy. Price, stock and consent are validated server-side. Social publishing and campaign attribution require approved APIs and opt-in rules.

title: Shelf and interest intelligence
source: I Shelf and Customer Interest Intelligence
statement: The platform shall relate anonymous zone/product interactions to shelf observations and aggregate sales.
accept: Define zone-to-SKU mappings and labeled product-facing data; measure gaps/misplacement precision. Aggregate interest-to-purchase with time/window rules; never equate anonymous tracks with identified customers.

title: Context signals and risk
statement: Approved weather, holiday, trend and sensor inputs shall be versioned, time-aligned and evaluated before influencing recommendations.
accept: Use only information available at prediction time. Missing feeds degrade gracefully. Pest outputs are inspection-risk recommendations, never confirmation. Staffing, delivery and cash-flow forecasts need separate targets.

title: Platform administration
source: I Organization and Store Management; Administration Reliability and System Operations
statement: Administrators shall manage branch configuration, devices, feature flags, credentials, retention and service health.
accept: Scope settings to authorized tenants; redact credentials; log changes. Subscription plans, business registration, operating hours, warehouses and device registration are not supplied by free-text selectors.
